title: Creamy banana porridge
summary: Smooth, slow-cooked oats with mashed banana and a little honey.
steps: Put the oats and milk in a small pan over a low heat.
Mash half the banana and stir it in.
Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and very soft. Add a splash more milk if needed.
Top with the rest of the banana, sliced, plus the honey and cinnamon.
tip: Cook the oats well so they're soft. If oats bother you, use fine 'instant' oats or ready brek-style oats, which are smoother.
swaps: Use stewed pear instead of banana
Use oat or soya milk

storage.text: Best fresh. Leftovers keep in a covered bowl in the fridge for 1 day — loosen with milk and reheat until piping hot.

title: Soft scrambled eggs on toast
summary: Silky, buttery scrambled eggs on white sourdough.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat.
Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula until just set and creamy.
Toast the bread and spoon the eggs on top.
tip: White sourdough is lower in fibre than wholemeal or seeded bread, and usually has a short ingredient list.
swaps: Serve on a soft white roll or crumpet

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Scrambled eggs go rubbery when stored and reheated.

title: Banana & peanut butter smoothie
summary: A filling, protein-rich smoothie that's easy on the gut.
steps: Put everything in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Drink straight away.
tip: Use smooth nut butter only — crunchy has nut pieces. Look for jars that are just peanuts (and maybe salt).
swaps: Use smooth almond butter or tahini instead of peanut butter

storage.text: Best fresh. Can be kept in a sealed bottle in the fridge for up to 1 day — shake before drinking.

title: Yoghurt with stewed pear
summary: Peeled pears gently cooked with cinnamon, spooned over thick yoghurt.
steps: Peel and core the pears, then cut into small pieces.
Put in a pan with the water, honey and cinnamon.
Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until very soft. Mash lightly if you like.
Spoon over the yoghurt, warm or cold.
tip: Peeling and cooking fruit removes the tough skin and softens the fibre.

storage.text: Stew a big batch of pears. Keep in a sealed tub in the fridge for 3 days, or freeze in portions for 3 months. Add the yoghurt when serving.

title: Fluffy banana pancakes
summary: Simple homemade pancakes sweetened with ripe banana.
ingredients: Maple syrup and sliced banana, to serve
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl, then whisk in the eggs and milk.
Stir in the flour until just combined.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick pan over a medium heat.
Add small ladles of batter and cook for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve with maple syrup and banana.
tip: Homemade pancakes avoid the additives found in many shop-bought ones.

storage.text: Cool, then stack with baking paper between. Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in a toaster or dry pan.

title: Mild shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smooth, mildly spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
ingredients: 1 red pepper, peeled and finely chopped
steps: Peel the pepper with a vegetable peeler (or use jarred roasted peppers, which peel easily).
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil over a low heat for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the cumin and paprika for 1 minute, then the passata. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender if you like.
Make 4 hollows and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set.
Crumble over the feta and serve with bread.
tip: Passata has no tomato skins or seeds, unlike tinned chopped tomatoes. Sweet paprika keeps it mild.
swaps: Use crumbled firm tofu instead of eggs

storage.text: Batch-cook the sauce only: fridge for 2 days or freeze for 3 months. Cook fresh eggs in the reheated sauce.

title: Cheese & spinach omelette
summary: A soft, folded omelette with wilted, finely chopped spinach and cheddar.
steps: Wilt the spinach in the pan with a splash of water, then chop it very finely.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan, add the eggs and swirl.
When almost set, add the spinach and cheese to one half, fold over and cook for 1 more minute.
tip: Chopping cooked spinach finely breaks up the stringy leaves.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away.

title: Carrot & ginger soup
summary: Bright, silky carrot soup with a gentle warmth from fresh ginger.
ingredients: Thumb-sized piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated
2 tbsp crème fraîche or a splash of milk
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the crème fraîche.
tip: Blending makes soups one of the easiest ways to eat veg with strictures. Choose a stock with a short ingredient list, or make your own.
swaps: Use a little ground ginger if fresh is too strong

storage.text: Cool quickly, then fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Add the crème fraîche after reheating.

title: Butternut squash soup
summary: Velvety roasted squash soup — sweet, smooth and comforting.
ingredients: 1 butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cubed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the squash and onion in the oil and roast for 25 minutes until soft.
Tip into a pan with the stock and nutmeg and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until silky smooth. Stir in the cream if using.
tip: Make sure every squash seed is scooped out before roasting.

storage.text: Cool quickly, then fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Add any cream after reheating.

title: Red lentil & carrot soup
summary: A filling, protein-rich soup that blends to a smooth finish.
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, then add the lentils and stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils have fallen apart.
Blend smooth and add a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Red lentils are split and skinless, so they're much gentler than whole beans. Start with small portions if pulses are new to you.
swaps: Add a peeled sweet potato for a sweeter soup

storage.text: Thickens as it stands. Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months; loosen with water when reheating.

title: Tomato soup & grilled cheese
summary: Smooth homemade tomato soup with a golden cheese toastie for dipping.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes.
Add the passata, stock and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend smooth and stir in the cream.
Butter the outside of the bread, fill with cheese and cook in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes each side until golden.
tip: Homemade soup avoids the thickeners and additives in many tinned soups.

storage.text: Batch-cook the soup: fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Make the toastie fresh.

title: Potato & leek soup
summary: A classic creamy soup, blended until totally smooth.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the leeks gently for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Add the milk and blend until completely smooth. Season to taste.
tip: Use only the pale part of the leek — the dark green tops are tougher and more fibrous.

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Potato soup can go a little grainy when frozen — blend again after reheating.

title: Hummus & roast pepper wrap
summary: Soft tortilla with smooth hummus, peeled roast peppers and feta.
ingredients: 3 tbsp smooth hummus (see the homemade hummus recipe)
2 jarred roasted red peppers, skins removed
Few leaves of soft butter lettuce, finely shredded (optional)
steps: Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for a few seconds.
Spread with hummus.
Slice the peppers into strips, checking for any skin, and lay them on top.
Crumble over the feta, roll up tightly and cut in half.
tip: Leave out the lettuce on harder days. Jarred peppers are already cooked and peel easily.

storage.text: Best made fresh. Can be wrapped and kept in the fridge until the next day.

title: Egg mayo sandwich
summary: Soft-boiled eggs mashed with mayo and chives on soft white bread.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Mash with the mayo, yoghurt, chives, salt and pepper.
Spread between the bread and cut into halves.
tip: Pick a mayonnaise with a short ingredient list, or mix half-and-half with yoghurt.

storage.text: Keep the egg mayo filling in a sealed tub in the fridge for 2 days. Make sandwiches fresh. Don't freeze.

title: Courgette & feta fritters
summary: Golden fritters made with peeled, grated courgette and salty feta.
ingredients: Small handful of mint or dill, finely chopped
steps: Grate the peeled courgettes, then squeeze out as much water as you can in a clean tea towel.
Mix with the feta, eggs, flour and herbs.
Heat oil in a frying pan and add spoonfuls of the mix, flattening slightly.
Cook for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Serve with yoghurt.
tip: Peeling courgettes removes the tougher skin; the soft flesh is usually well tolerated when cooked.

storage.text: Cool, then fridge for 2 days or freeze between baking paper for 2 months. Reheat in the oven until hot all the way through.

title: Avocado & egg on toast
summary: Smashed avocado with a squeeze of lemon and a soft poached egg.
steps: Mash the avocado with the lemon, salt and pepper until smooth.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 minutes.
Toast the bread, spread with avocado and top with the eggs.
tip: Skip chilli flakes and seeds that are often added to this dish.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away — avocado browns quickly.

title: Butternut squash dhal
summary: Mild, creamy red lentil dhal with soft squash and coconut milk.
ingredients: 300g butternut squash, peeled and diced small
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, squash, coconut milk and stock.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the squash breaks up.
Mash or blend some of it for a smoother texture. Serve with rice.
tip: No chilli — the flavour comes from warming spices instead. White rice is lower in fibre than brown.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Great for batch cooking. Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Cook rice fresh, or see the rice note below.

title: Butternut squash risotto
summary: Creamy risotto with soft roasted squash and parmesan-style cheese.
steps: Roast the squash in the oil at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes. Mash half of it.
Meanwhile, melt the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the mashed squash, the cubes and the cheese. Rest for 2 minutes before serving.
tip: Traditional parmesan isn't vegetarian — look for a vegetarian hard cheese. Risotto rice is soft and low in fibre.

storage.text: Risotto contains rice, so cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Lemon & spinach risotto
summary: Fresh, bright risotto with wilted spinach blended into the rice.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18–20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wilt the spinach and blend it with a splash of stock to a smooth purée.
Stir the spinach purée, lemon, cheese and mascarpone into the rice.
tip: Blending the spinach gives you the greens without the stringy leaves.

storage.text: Risotto contains rice, so cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Butternut mac & cheese
summary: Homemade cheese sauce with puréed squash hidden inside.
steps: Boil the squash for 12 minutes until soft, then mash or blend smooth.
Cook the macaroni until soft. Drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in the squash, most of the cheese, the mustard and nutmeg.
Mix with the pasta, top with the rest of the cheese and grill until bubbling.
tip: Cook pasta a little past al dente on harder days — softer pasta is easier to digest.
swaps: Use peeled sweet potato instead of squash

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze in portions for 2 months. Add a splash of milk when reheating.

title: Sticky honey-soy tofu with rice
summary: Crispy tofu in a sticky, garlicky glaze with soft carrots and rice.
steps: Toss the tofu in the cornflour.
Fry in the oil for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden.
Steam or boil the carrots for 8 minutes until very soft.
Mix the soy, honey, garlic and ginger, pour into the pan and bubble until sticky.
Serve over rice with the carrots.
tip: Leave off the sesame seeds that usually top this dish. Plain tofu is a minimally processed protein.
swaps: Use maple syrup to make it vegan

storage.text: Store the tofu and carrots for 2 days in the fridge. Cooked rice must be cooled within 1 hour and eaten within 1 day.

title: Mild butter paneer
summary: Paneer in a smooth, creamy tomato sauce — all flavour, no heat.
ingredients: White basmati rice or plain naan, to serve
steps: Fry the paneer in half the butter until golden. Set aside.
Melt the rest of the butter and soften the onion for 8 minutes. Add garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the passata and simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream, honey and paneer and heat through.
tip: Leave out chilli and fresh green chillies. Blending the sauce removes onion pieces.
swaps: Use firm tofu instead of paneer
Use coconut milk instead of cream

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. The sauce freezes well; add a splash of cream when reheating.

title: Gnocchi & mozzarella bake
summary: Soft potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with melting mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Warm the oil and garlic, add the passata and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi for 2 minutes until they float. Drain and stir into the sauce.
Tip into a baking dish, top with mozzarella and bake for 15 minutes until bubbling.
tip: Choose gnocchi with a short ingredient list (mostly potato and flour), or make your own.

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Gnocchi goes soft when frozen, but you can freeze the sauce on its own for 3 months.

title: Lentil shepherd's pie
summary: Rich red lentil and carrot filling under fluffy, buttery mash.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetarian Worcestershire sauce or soy sauce
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the lentils, tomato purée, Worcestershire, stock and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until soft and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the filling into a dish, top with mash and cheese.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes until golden.
tip: No peas here (a common stricture risk). Standard Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies — use a vegetarian one or soy.
swaps: Top with mashed sweet potato instead

storage.text: Ideal for batch cooking. Fridge for 3 days or freeze (whole or in portions) for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight, then reheat until piping hot.

title: Cauliflower cheese
summary: Tender cauliflower in a golden, bubbling cheddar sauce.
ingredients: 1 cauliflower, cut into small florets (stalks removed)
steps: Boil the florets for 8–10 minutes until very tender. Drain well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Pour over the cauliflower, top with the rest of the cheese and grill until golden.
tip: Use only the florets and cook them until very soft. Cauliflower can cause wind for some people, so try a small portion first.

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in the oven until bubbling.

title: Halloumi & peeled veg traybake
summary: Roasted sweet potato, carrots and courgette with golden halloumi.
ingredients: 3 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 courgette, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the veg with oil and oregano on a large tray and roast for 30 minutes.
Add the halloumi slices and roast for 10–15 minutes more until golden.
Finish with lemon.
tip: Roast until the veg is soft all the way through, not crunchy at the edges.
swaps: Use firm tofu or paneer instead of halloumi

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Halloumi goes rubbery if frozen, but the roast veg alone freezes for 2 months.

title: Simple egg fried rice
summary: Quick fried rice with egg and soft carrot — no peas or sweetcorn.
ingredients: 1 spring onion, green part only, finely sliced
steps: Heat the oil in a wok and cook the grated carrot for 2–3 minutes until soft.
Push to one side, add the eggs and scramble.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir-fry until piping hot.
Scatter over the spring onion.
tip: Shop and takeaway versions usually include peas and sweetcorn — making it yourself avoids both.
swaps: Add cubes of firm tofu for extra protein

storage.text: Cool within 1 hour, fridge, and eat within 1 day. Reheat only once, until steaming hot. Don't freeze.

title: Creamy roast pepper pasta
summary: Pasta in a silky blended sauce of roast peppers and cream cheese.
steps: Cook the pasta. Keep a cup of the water.
Blend the peppers, garlic, cream cheese and hard cheese until very smooth.
Warm the sauce in the pan, loosening with pasta water.
Toss with the pasta and top with basil.
tip: Blending the peppers removes any bits of skin.
swaps: Use ricotta instead of cream cheese

storage.text: Batch-make the sauce: fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Cooked pasta with sauce keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Spinach & ricotta pasta bake
summary: Pasta shells baked with tomato sauce, creamy ricotta and blended spinach.
steps: Cook the pasta until soft. Drain.
Wilt the spinach, squeeze dry and blend or chop very finely. Mix with the ricotta, egg and nutmeg.
Warm the passata with the garlic for 5 minutes.
Mix the pasta with the sauce, dollop over the ricotta mix and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes.
tip: Finely chopped or blended spinach is easier to digest than whole leaves.

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat covered in the oven until hot all the way through.

title: Miso noodle soup with tofu
summary: A light, soothing broth with soft noodles and silken tofu.
ingredients: 1 carrot, peeled and cut into thin ribbons
1 spring onion, green part only, finely sliced
steps: Bring the water to a simmer with the ginger and carrot. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook as the packet says.
Turn off the heat, then whisk in the miso and soy.
Add the tofu gently and serve topped with spring onion.
tip: Don't boil the miso — add it off the heat. Udon noodles are soft and low in fibre.

storage.text: Best fresh. The broth (without noodles or tofu) keeps 1 day in the fridge.

title: Mild sweet potato & coconut curry
summary: A gentle, creamy curry with peeled sweet potato and spinach.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, coconut milk and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Serve with rice.
tip: Pick a 'mild' curry powder and check it has no chilli listed high up.
swaps: Use butternut squash instead of sweet potato

storage.text: Great for batch cooking. Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Cook rice fresh.

title: Creamy baked eggs
summary: Eggs baked in little dishes with cream, spinach purée and cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter 2 ramekins.
Divide the spinach between them, crack 2 eggs into each and spoon over the cream.
Top with cheese and bake for 12–15 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve with toast for dipping.
tip: A quick, soft, high-protein meal for days when you don't feel like much.

storage.text: Best eaten straight away.

title: Cheesy polenta with tomato sauce
summary: Soft, creamy polenta topped with a slow-simmered smooth tomato sauce.
steps: Warm the oil and garlic, add the passata and simmer for 15 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil and whisk in the polenta. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick.
Beat in the butter and cheese.
Spoon into bowls and top with the sauce and basil.
tip: Polenta is made from finely ground corn, without the tough husks of whole sweetcorn kernels. Try a small portion first.

storage.text: Polenta sets firm in the fridge (2 days) — slice and fry it, or reheat with milk. The tomato sauce freezes for 3 months.

title: Stewed apple & custard
summary: Soft cinnamon apple with simple homemade custard.
steps: Simmer the apples, sugar, cinnamon and water with a lid on for 10 minutes until soft.
For the custard, heat the milk until steaming.
Whisk the yolks, sugar, cornflour and vanilla, then slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Return to the pan and stir over a low heat until thick. Pour over the apples.
tip: Homemade custard avoids colourings and thickeners in many ready-made versions.

storage.text: Stewed apple keeps 3 days in the fridge or freezes for 3 months. Custard keeps 2 days in the fridge — don't freeze it.

title: Creamy rice pudding
summary: Slow-cooked pudding rice in vanilla milk — pure comfort.
steps: Put the rice, milk, sugar and vanilla in a pan.
Simmer very gently for 30–35 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the butter and top with nutmeg.
tip: Very gentle and filling — a good choice during a flare.
swaps: Use oat or soya milk and maple syrup to make it vegan

storage.text: Cool within 1 hour and fridge for up to 2 days. Eat cold, or reheat once until hot. Don't freeze.

title: Simple banana bread
summary: Moist, nut-free banana bread with a short, simple ingredient list.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas, then stir in the butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Fold in the bicarb, salt and flour.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
tip: No walnuts or seeds — just plain banana bread.
swaps: Use oil instead of butter

storage.text: Keep wrapped at room temperature for 3 days. Freeze whole or in slices for 3 months.

title: Silky homemade hummus
summary: Extra-smooth hummus with warm pitta for dipping.
steps: For the smoothest hummus, pinch the skins off the chickpeas (or simmer them for 10 minutes with ½ tsp bicarb, then rinse).
Blend the tahini and lemon first until creamy.
Add the chickpeas, garlic and oil, and blend for 3–4 minutes, adding water until silky.
Serve with warm pitta.
tip: Removing the chickpea skins and blending for longer gives a much smoother result. Tahini is smooth ground sesame, not whole seeds.

storage.text: Keep in a sealed tub in the fridge for 3 days, or freeze for 2 months. Stir well after thawing.

title: Banana oat breakfast bars
summary: Soft, nut-free baked oat bars — grab one on the way out or pack for later.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mash the bananas, then beat in the eggs, milk and honey.
Stir in the oats, cinnamon and baking powder.
Spread into the tin and bake for 25 minutes until set and golden.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 8 bars.
tip: No nuts, seeds or dried fruit. Blitz the oats first for a smoother bar.
swaps: Use maple syrup instead of honey
Use any milk, including oat milk

storage.text: Keep in a sealed tub in the fridge for 3 days, or wrap bars individually and freeze for 3 months. Thaw overnight or warm for 20 seconds in the microwave.

title: Peanut butter overnight oats
summary: Five-ingredient oats that soften overnight — breakfast is ready when you wake.
steps: Stir everything together in a jar or bowl.
Cover and chill overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
Stir and add a splash more milk if it's too thick. Eat cold or warm it through.
tip: Soaking makes oats very soft. Use smooth nut butter only.
swaps: Swap peanut butter for smooth almond butter or tahini
Use plant yoghurt and milk to make it vegan

storage.text: Make 2 jars at once — they keep for 2 days in the fridge. Don't freeze.

title: Mango & silken tofu smoothie
summary: Creamy, dairy-free and packed with protein from silken tofu.
steps: Put everything in a blender.
Blend for a full minute until completely smooth.
Drink straight away.
tip: Mango and banana have no seeds or tough skins once peeled. Silken tofu blends invisibly.
swaps: Use soya milk and maple syrup for a vegan version

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps in a sealed bottle in the fridge for 1 day — shake well.

title: Cinnamon French toast with apple
summary: Golden eggy bread with soft, buttery cinnamon apples.
steps: Cook the apples in a little butter with half the cinnamon for 8–10 minutes until very soft.
Whisk the eggs, milk and remaining cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Soak each slice of bread for a few seconds on each side.
Fry in butter over a medium heat for 2–3 minutes each side until golden.
Serve topped with the apples and honey.
tip: Peeling and cooking the apple removes the skin and softens the fibre.
swaps: Use pears instead of apples
Use stewed pear or banana if apple doesn't suit you

storage.text: Best fresh. Cooked French toast can be frozen for 1 month and reheated in a toaster. The apples keep 3 days in the fridge.

title: Cottage cheese pancakes
summary: Light, high-protein pancakes blended smooth with cottage cheese.
ingredients: Sliced banana or stewed pear, to serve
steps: Blend the cottage cheese and eggs until smooth.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick pan over a medium-low heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for 2 minutes each side until golden and set.
Serve with banana or stewed pear.
tip: Blending the cottage cheese gives a smooth batter and adds plenty of protein.
swaps: Use ricotta instead of cottage cheese

storage.text: Cool, then stack with baking paper between. Fridge for 2 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in a toaster or dry pan.

title: Cheese & courgette egg muffins
summary: Baked mini omelettes — perfect for lunchboxes and busy mornings.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 6-hole muffin tin.
Squeeze the grated courgette dry in a clean tea towel.
Beat the eggs and milk, then stir in the courgette, cheese and chives.
Pour into the tin and bake for 18–20 minutes until set in the middle.
Cool for 5 minutes before lifting out.
tip: Peeled, grated and baked courgette is very soft. Squeezing out the water stops them going soggy.
swaps: Use wilted, finely chopped spinach instead of courgette
Use feta instead of cheddar

storage.text: Fridge in a sealed tub for 3 days, or freeze for 2 months. Reheat until piping hot, or eat cold from the fridge within 3 days.

title: Cauliflower & cheddar soup
summary: Like cauliflower cheese in a bowl — velvety, comforting and rich in calcium.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the potato, cauliflower and stock. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until very soft.
Add the milk and blend until completely smooth.
Stir in the cheese and mustard over a low heat until melted.
tip: Cauliflower can cause wind for some people — start with a small bowl.
swaps: Use broccoli florets (no stalks) instead of half the cauliflower

storage.text: Freeze before adding the cheese for the best texture, then stir it in when reheating. Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months.

title: Silky spinach & potato soup
summary: A bright green soup that gets spinach in without any stringy leaves.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted.
Blend until completely smooth, then add nutmeg and crème fraîche.
tip: Blending the spinach fully gives you its iron without the stringy texture.
swaps: Use a splash of oat cream to make it dairy-free

storage.text: Cool quickly, then fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Add the crème fraîche after reheating.

title: Red pepper & butter bean soup
summary: Sweet, smoky and creamy, with blended butter beans for protein.
ingredients: 400g tin butter beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the peppers, butter beans and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend for 2–3 minutes until completely smooth.
For extra smoothness, push through a sieve to catch any bean skins.
tip: Whole beans have tough skins, so blend this very well and sieve if you're unsure. Try a small portion first.
swaps: Use cannellini beans instead of butter beans

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Loosen with a little water when reheating.

title: Ginger egg drop soup
summary: A light, soothing broth with silky ribbons of egg — ready in minutes.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 spring onion, green part only, finely sliced
steps: Simmer the stock, ginger and soy sauce for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornflour mix and simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir the soup in a circle and slowly pour in the eggs in a thin stream.
Leave for 30 seconds, then stir gently. Top with spring onion.
tip: Very gentle and quick to make — a good choice on a flare day.
swaps: Add cubes of silken tofu for extra protein
Add a nest of soft udon noodles to make it more filling

storage.text: Best fresh. Leftovers keep 1 day in the fridge — reheat gently until steaming.

title: Cheese & chive potato cakes
summary: Crisp outside, fluffy inside — a great use for leftover mash.
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Boil the potatoes until very soft. Drain well and mash smooth.
Mix in the cheese, egg yolk, chives and flour. Season.
With floured hands, shape into 8 cakes.
Fry in a little oil and butter for 3–4 minutes each side until golden.
tip: Peeled, well-mashed potato is one of the gentlest starchy foods.
swaps: Use mashed sweet potato for half the potato

storage.text: Freeze uncooked cakes between baking paper for 3 months and fry from frozen (add a few minutes). Cooked cakes keep 2 days in the fridge.

title: Soft egg & onion rice bowl
summary: Japanese-style eggs gently set in a sweet soy broth over white rice.
ingredients: 1 spring onion, green part only, sliced
steps: Simmer the onion in the stock, soy and honey for 8–10 minutes until very soft.
Pour the eggs over the onions. Cover and cook on a low heat for 2–3 minutes until just set.
Slide on to bowls of hot rice and top with spring onion.
tip: Simmering the onion until very soft makes it much easier to digest.
swaps: Add cubes of firm tofu with the onion

storage.text: Best eaten straight away. Cook rice fresh, or cool leftover rice within 1 hour and eat within 1 day.

title: Spanish potato tortilla
summary: A thick, soft potato omelette — good hot, cold or in a lunchbox.
steps: Cook the potatoes and onion gently in the oil in a 20cm non-stick pan for 20 minutes, until very soft but not browned.
Drain off most of the oil. Beat the eggs with salt and stir in the potatoes.
Return to the pan and cook on a low heat for 8–10 minutes until almost set.
Flip on to a plate, slide back in and cook for 3–4 minutes more.
tip: Cooking the potato and onion slowly until soft keeps it gentle.
swaps: Leave out the onion if it doesn't suit you

storage.text: Cool, wrap and keep in the fridge for 3 days. Eat cold or warm gently. Don't freeze — the egg goes watery.

title: Red lentil bolognese
summary: A rich, family-friendly ragu that freezes brilliantly.
ingredients: Vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, to serve
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, passata, tomato purée, stock and oregano.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the lentils have broken down.
Cook the spaghetti until soft and serve with the sauce and cheese.
tip: Grated carrot and red lentils melt into the sauce. Blend half for a smoother texture.
swaps: Use any pasta shape
Serve over mashed potato instead of pasta

storage.text: Freeze the sauce in portions for 3 months, or fridge for 3 days. Cook pasta fresh.

title: Mild tofu & spinach korma
summary: A creamy, gently spiced curry with no nuts and no chilli.
steps: Fry the tofu in the oil until golden. Set aside.
Soften the onion for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes, then blend smooth.
Stir in the spinach and tofu. Take off the heat and stir in the yoghurt.
Serve with rice.
tip: Korma is usually thickened with nuts — this version uses blended onion and yoghurt instead.
swaps: Use paneer instead of tofu
Use coconut yoghurt to make it vegan

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. Reheat gently — don't let it boil after the yoghurt goes in.

title: Lentil & squash lasagne
summary: Layers of soft lentil ragu, squash and creamy white sauce — a freezer favourite.
ingredients: 1 batch red lentil bolognese sauce (see that recipe)
300g butternut squash, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Make a white sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick. Stir in half the cheese.
Layer the ragu, lasagne sheets, squash slices and white sauce in a large dish, three times, finishing with white sauce.
Top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 45 minutes until the pasta and squash are soft. Rest for 10 minutes.
tip: Thin squash slices bake until very tender. Check with a knife before serving.
swaps: Use courgette (peeled) instead of squash

storage.text: Freeze whole or in portions for 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight, then reheat covered until piping hot.

title: Cheesy leek & potato gratin
summary: Thin potato slices baked in garlicky cream with soft leeks and cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Soften the leeks in the butter for 10 minutes.
Warm the cream, milk and garlic. Layer the potatoes and leeks in a dish.
Pour over the cream and top with cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover for 15 minutes until golden and soft.
tip: Rich, so keep portions moderate if high-fat food bothers you.
swaps: Use half stock, half milk for a lighter version

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days or freeze in portions for 2 months. Reheat covered in the oven.

title: Saag paneer
summary: Paneer in a smooth, buttery spinach sauce — iron and protein together.
ingredients: White basmati rice or plain naan, to serve
steps: Fry the paneer in half the butter until golden. Set aside.
Soften the onion in the rest of the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the spinach in batches until wilted.
Blend the sauce until completely smooth.
Stir in the cream and paneer and heat through.
tip: Blending makes the spinach smooth. No chilli — warmth comes from ginger and cumin.
swaps: Use firm tofu instead of paneer

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months. The paneer may firm up slightly after freezing.

title: Mild egg & tomato curry
summary: Soft-boiled eggs in a smooth, fragrant tomato and coconut sauce.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder.
Add the passata and coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend smooth.
Halve the eggs, add to the sauce and warm through. Serve with rice.
tip: Check your curry powder is labelled mild and has no chilli high on the list.
swaps: Add cubes of peeled sweet potato to bulk it out

storage.text: Freeze the sauce on its own for 3 months and add freshly boiled eggs. With eggs, keep in the fridge for up to 2 days.

title: Courgette & ricotta pasta
summary: Five ingredients, twenty minutes — silky, lemony and very gentle.
steps: Cook the pasta until soft. Keep a cup of the water.
Cook the courgettes in the butter for 8 minutes until very soft.
Stir in the ricotta, lemon zest and a splash of pasta water to make a creamy sauce.
Toss with the pasta and season.
tip: Peeled, well-cooked courgette is one of the easiest vegetables to tolerate.
swaps: Add grated vegetarian hard cheese on top
Use cream cheese instead of ricotta

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when reheating. Don't freeze.

title: Slow-cooker lentil & sweet potato stew
summary: Fifteen minutes of prep, then it cooks itself. Makes six freezer portions.
steps: Put everything except the lemon into a slow cooker.
Cook on low for 6–8 hours, or high for 4 hours, until everything is very soft.
Mash or blend some of it for a thicker, smoother stew.
Add lemon and season before serving.
tip: Slow cooking breaks vegetables down until they're very tender. The 15 minutes is hands-on time — total cooking time is 4–8 hours.
swaps: No slow cooker? Simmer in a covered pan for 40 minutes, stirring often.

storage.text: Fridge for 3 days or freeze in portions for 3 months. Loosen with water when reheating.

title: Creamy baked feta pasta
summary: A block of feta baked in passata, then stirred into a creamy sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Pour the passata into a baking dish, stir in the garlic and oil, and put the feta in the middle.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta until soft.
Mash the feta into the sauce, then stir in the pasta and basil.
tip: The viral version uses cherry tomatoes, which have skins and seeds. Passata gives the same flavour without them.
swaps: Stir in wilted, finely chopped spinach

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water. The sauce alone freezes for 2 months.

title: Spinach & feta filo pie
summary: Golden filo layers over a soft, cheesy spinach and egg filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Wilt the spinach, squeeze out the water and chop very finely.
Mix with the feta, ricotta, eggs and nutmeg.
Line a dish with 3 buttered filo sheets, add the filling and top with 3 more buttered sheets, scrunched.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and set.
tip: Leave off the sesame seeds often scattered on top. Chew the crisp filo well.
swaps: Use cheddar instead of feta for a milder flavour

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days, or freeze (baked) for 2 months. Reheat in the oven so the pastry crisps up.

title: Silky chocolate pots
summary: Three ingredients — rich chocolate mousse made with silken tofu.
steps: Blend the tofu until completely smooth.
Add the melted chocolate and maple syrup and blend again.
Spoon into small pots and chill for at least 1 hour.
tip: A smooth, protein-rich pudding. Dark chocolate has some caffeine, so go easy if that affects you.
swaps: Use milk chocolate for a milder flavour

storage.text: Cover and keep in the fridge for 3 days. Don't freeze.

title: Banana & peanut butter ice cream
summary: Two-ingredient soft-serve made from frozen banana.
steps: Let the frozen banana sit for 5 minutes.
Blend with the peanut butter, scraping down the sides, until smooth and creamy.
Eat straight away as soft-serve, or freeze for 1 hour for a firmer scoop.
tip: Freeze ripe bananas in slices so they're always ready.
swaps: Leave out the peanut butter, or swap for 1 tbsp cocoa powder

storage.text: Best eaten fresh. Freeze leftovers in a tub for up to 1 month — let it soften for 10 minutes before scooping.

title: Baked egg custard
summary: A classic, wobbly vanilla custard with nutmeg — soft, simple and nourishing.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Warm the milk until steaming. Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla, then whisk in the milk.
Strain into an ovenproof dish and grate over nutmeg.
Stand the dish in a roasting tin half-filled with hot water.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
tip: Gentle protein and calcium for days when eating feels hard.
swaps: Add a strip of lemon zest to the milk while it warms

storage.text: Cool, cover and keep in the fridge for 2 days. Eat cold. Don't freeze.

title: Semolina pudding with jam
summary: Creamy, comforting semolina with a swirl of seedless jam.
steps: Warm the milk in a pan.
Whisk in the semolina and sugar.
Simmer, stirring constantly, for 8–10 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir in the vanilla and serve with a spoonful of jam.
tip: Choose seedless jam (such as apricot or seedless raspberry) to avoid tiny seeds.
swaps: Use stewed pear or apple instead of jam

storage.text: Fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of milk. Don't freeze.

title: Apple & cinnamon muffins
summary: Soft, nut-free muffins with peeled, grated apple.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, cinnamon, bicarb and sugar.
Beat the eggs, milk and butter, then stir into the dry mix with the apple until just combined.
Divide between the cases and bake for 20 minutes until risen and golden.
tip: Grated, peeled apple bakes right into the crumb — no chunks or skin.
swaps: Use peeled pear instead of apple

storage.text: Keep in a tin for 3 days, or freeze for 3 months. Thaw at room temperature or warm for 15 seconds.

title: Cheese scones
summary: Fluffy, savoury scones — great with soup or in a lunchbox.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a baking tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and baking powder until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in most of the cheese and the mustard, then the milk, to make a soft dough.
Pat out to 2.5cm thick, cut into 8 rounds and brush with milk. Top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until risen and golden.
tip: White flour scones are lower in fibre than wholemeal ones.
swaps: Add 1 tbsp snipped chives to the dough

storage.text: Best on the day. Keep in a tin for 2 days, or freeze for 3 months and warm through in the oven.

title: Mango lassi
summary: A cool, creamy yoghurt drink with sweet mango.
steps: Blend everything until completely smooth.
Taste and add more honey if needed. Serve chilled.
tip: Natural yoghurt with live cultures — a gentle, calcium-rich snack.
swaps: Use soya yoghurt and milk to make it dairy-free

storage.text: Best fresh. Keeps 1 day in a sealed bottle in the fridge — shake before drinking.
